title: Restriction of a quotient by an fppf relation is an open subspace
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U,R,U'$ be schemes over $S$, and let $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] be an equivalence relation: for every $S$-scheme $T$, $j$ identifies $R(T)$ with an equivalence relation on $U(T)$. Suppose $s,t:R\to U$ are surjective, flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $g:U'\to U$ be flat and locally of finite presentation, and let $R'=U'\times_{g,U,s}R\times_{t,U,g}U'$ be the restricted relation. On the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], let $F=U/R$ and $F'=U'/R'$ be the sheafifications [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $T\mapsto U(T)/R(T)$ and $T\mapsto U'(T)/R'(T)$. The canonical map $F'\to F$ is representable and an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]: for every $S$-scheme $T$ and $a:h_T\to F$, the pullback $h_T\times_F F'$ is represented by an open subscheme of $T$.

source.place: Tag 02WU (finding-opens), using Tag 02VH for restriction of the relation and Tags 023Q/02W2 for fppf descent of opens

proof.text: Construct the canonical map alpha: the two pullback equations identify the composites of the restricted projections with g with maps through s and t. Their Yoneda maps therefore coequalize after the quotient map q. Apply the presheaf coequalizer and then the universal property of the given sheafification F prime. This proves exactly the displayed compatibility.

source.place: Tag 02WU, canonical map from the restricted quotient; Groupoids Tag 045Z

proof.text: Derive local surjectivity of each given sheafification unit directly from its universal property: form the subsheaf locally generated by its image. Universality gives a map from the sheaf to this subsheaf; uniqueness shows that its composite with the inclusion is the identity. Hence the subsheaf is the whole sheaf. Presheaf coequalizer projections are sectionwise surjective (they are pointwise epimorphisms in Type), so q and q prime are locally surjective. This avoids any existence assumption for small-valued sheafification on the large big site.

source.place: Tag 02WU, local representatives; Sites Tag 00WK, local surjectivity via the image subsheaf

proof.text: Prove sectionwise injectivity of alpha. For two maps u,v:T to U prime with equal images in F, apply the kernel-pair pullback square [lem-trf-etale-relation-kernel-pair] to their Yoneda maps. Yoneda fullness gives r:T to R with endpoints ug and vg. Two pullback lifts give d:T to the restricted relation with endpoints u,v, so the restricted coequalizer sends u,v to the same section. For arbitrary sections x,y of F prime with equal images, intersect the covering image sieves of q prime at x,y. On each arrow choose representatives u,v. Naturality and canonical-map compatibility give equality of their images in F; the preceding argument makes the restrictions of x,y equal. Sheaf separation proves x=y.

Apply [lem-trf-relation-incidence-open-model] with alpha, its compatibility and its sectionwise injectivity. At v=identity on U its pullback square identifies the representable of the incidence open W with h_U times_F F prime, over h_U.

source.place: Tag 02WU, incidence open and representing property over the atlas

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fppf-local-open-subfunctor-descent] using local surjectivity of q and the open-model isomorphism from the preceding step. For every test T and section a it gives an open V and an isomorphism h_V to h_T times_F F prime compatible with the projection. The standard pullback square transported along this isomorphism, then flipped, is exactly the witness required by IsRepresentableWith. The inclusion of V is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 02WU, descent of opens to every test scheme

proof_origin.place: Tag 02WU and Groupoids Tag 045Z, using the stated incidence-open and local-open-descent theorems. The local-surjectivity glue is proved directly from the given sheafification universal property by the image-subsheaf argument (Sites Tag 00WK).

lean.statement: theorem etale_relation_finding_opens {S : Scheme.{u}} {R U U' : Over S} (s t : R ⟶ U) [Mono (prod.lift s t)] (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ U ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) [Surjective s.left] [Flat s.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation s.left] [Surjective t.left] [Flat t.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation t.left] (g : U' ⟶ U) [Flat g.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation g.left] (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (η : coequalizer (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ⟶ F.obj) (hη : ∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun k : F.obj ⟶ G.obj ↦ η ≫ k)) (F' : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (η' : coequalizer (yoneda.map (pullback.fst (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g ≫ pullback.fst g s)) (yoneda.map (pullback.snd (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g)) ⟶ F'.obj) (hη' : ∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun k : F'.obj ⟶ G.obj ↦ η' ≫ k)) : ∃ α : F'.obj ⟶ F.obj, (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map (pullback.fst (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g ≫ pullback.fst g s)) (yoneda.map (pullback.snd (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g)) ≫ η') ≫ α = yoneda.map g ≫ (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ≫ η) ∧ AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) α
